speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I need to examine you to understand your condition. How many days old are you, and do you have any fever, breathing difficulty, or poor feeding?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, female. The patient is a 3000-g (6.6-lb) female newborn delivered at term to a 23-year-old primigravida mother. The mother reports having had no prenatal care, and immunization records for the newborn are not available.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. I see you are a newborn female with no prenatal care and no immunization records. Do you have any jaundice, a swollen abdomen, or difficulty breathing?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Continuous heart murmur. I also have Bluish macules on the skin that do not blanch with pressure, Cloudy lenses in both eyes noticed upon examination, Failure to pass auditory screening tests.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Rubella Syndrome. The combination of a continuous heart murmur (suggesting Patent Ductus Arteriosus), bluish non-blanching macules (likely blueberry muffin rash), cloudy lenses (cataracts), and sensorineural deafness in a newborn with no immunization records is the classic triad of congenital rubella.
